answer: Each epoch, every identity is paired at random with a stranger from another orchard branch and must co-sign a small piece of fresh, unpredictable work. The kernel of trust is the record of these cross-pairings: a hollow identity with no pairings carries zero weight. Clones fail because a farm's outputs are statistically similar — the orchard's audit compares paired outputs, and when a cluster's work correlates, the whole cluster is pruned. Faking one identity costs one full set of distinct, real work; faking a hundred costs a hundred, with no pooling.
